Bully's legacy 

Act 1 – The Mystery

You play as the kid.

He’s tough, smart-mouthed, and clearly skilled beyond his years, but you don’t know why.

Missions feel like classic Bully chaos: school brawls, pranks, teacher dodge, rising tensions.

There’s whisper of his past, hints that he’s "not like the others."



---

Act 2 – The Reveal & Training

Mission 3: The rainy showdown where Jimmy saves the kid.
The reveal: He’s Jimmy Hopkins’ son.

Post-reveal, the next few missions become more character-driven:

Jimmy starts training him. Not just how to fight better, but also how to strategize, manipulate, survive.

Classic montage-style missions: boxing in garages, dodging school security, pranking high-level targets with precision.

Deep convos: Jimmy opens up about his past, his regrets, and how he never wanted his son to end up like him — but also knows the kid is made for this life.




---

Act 3 – Taking the Torch

The kid becomes the dominant figure in the school. He’s not just brawling now, he’s running schemes, making alliances, and taking on a new threat — maybe a private elite gang, or a corrupt adult force (like a new principal or underground crime ring).

Jimmy disappears from the story for a while — maybe sent away, or keeping a distance intentionally.



---

Final Mission – Father & Son

The climax: The school (or city) is under siege, chaos everywhere. The kid is surrounded.

Plot twist: A powerful enemy from Jimmy’s past resurfaces — someone Jimmy never finished with.

Just when things seem hopeless… Jimmy returns.

Side-by-side, father and son take on the final challenge together. Maybe even a dual playable mission: switching between them mid-fight.



---

Final Scene

Standing at the school gates, the kid looks at Jimmy:

“So what now?”

Jimmy smirks:
“Now? You run this place. I’m just the old guy in the leather jacket.”


Fade out with the school bell ringing.

A young man, his expression brimming with the hopeful enthusiasm of someone expecting to be rewarded for their journey, strides purposefully toward the kitchen. His stomach, a demanding and insistent organ, has led him to this moment, where he stands before the large, humming, rectangular bastion of cold preservation—the refrigerator. With a flourish of movement and the confidence of a man who believes in the power of past choices, he grips the handle and swings the door open, flooding his vision with the brilliant white light of its interior. His pupils adjust to the glow, scanning eagerly across the shelves, each level a stage upon which he anticipates a feast, a delicacy, or at the very least, a satisfying morsel.

But what meets his gaze is a desolate, barren landscape. The shelves, once laden with promise, now present only relics of past indulgence—a half-empty bottle of ketchup, a forgotten jar of pickles, a lone slice of processed cheese clinging to its plastic prison, and a carton of milk whose expiration date suggests it has seen better days. His breath catches as the weight of realization settles upon him. The bountiful treasure trove he had envisioned is, in fact, a graveyard of neglected condiments and unfulfilled desires.

His posture slackens, shoulders drooping under the crushing weight of disappointment. His eyes, once wide with optimism, now glaze over in the dull resignation of a man who has been here before—who will, inevitably, be here again. With a sigh, he reaches out, not to claim a prize, but to admit defeat. The door swings closed, the bright interior light extinguishing with a quiet click, leaving him once again in the dim, indifferent glow of the kitchen. He lingers for a moment, as if expecting some divine intervention, some forgotten snack to materialize in his time of need.

And then, without another word, he turns and walks away, carrying with him the bitter lesson of his futile pilgrimage: the fridge holds no miracles today.

The first official trailer for *Grand Theft Auto VI* (GTA VI) was released by Rockstar Games on December 5, 2023, after an early leak prompted them to release it ahead of schedule. The trailer confirmed that the game will be set in the iconic Vice City, a Miami-inspired location, and will feature a female protagonist named Lucia, marking a first for the series. The game is set to release in 2025, more than a decade after *GTA V* was launched in 2013.

As for the second trailer, there is no official release date yet. However, many fans speculate that it might drop in October 2024, following Rockstar's typical pattern of releasing trailers a year apart. This timing would also align with the potential announcement of other major gaming events and releases.

When you think of Rockstar Games, you think of quality content. When you think of GTA, you think of the best game ever made. It's a best-selling game that broke a lot of records and R* deserved it.... But that was almost 10 years ago. The mindset has changed a lot and the result can be seen today in GTA: The Trilogy: Definitive Edition. The goal of this remaster was to bring the classic titles to modern consoles and allow new players to enjoy the game as we did 20 years ago. But only in theory. What you get is actually not what you would expect from a GTA game, but the complete opposite. The graphics of the game seem new and beautiful for the first few minutes, but then you realize that the game hasn't been maintained at all. It's like "let's use Unreal because it has nice graphics, and just slap it on GTA III/VC/San Andreas" that's it. Sure, you can't just use a completely different engine, that requires some work.. Right? No, that's excatly how it looks like. All 3 games have the same bugs that you'd find in the original version of GTA. The remaster also introduced a lot of new bugs that just ruin the gameplay. The controls are really weird (especially in VC where it feels like you're playing the game on Stadia, Nvidia NOW, etc, but with a really bad internet connection). Some of the new textures are simply taken from GTA V, you can now see billboards with GTA: Online characters on them. A widescreen TV from the mid-2000s can now be found in GTA VC in Diaz mansion (the game is set in 1986).

And much more. That's just the tip of the iceberg, there's a lot more to tell, but I think most of it can easily be found on social media.

Would I recommend anyone to buy this game? No! If you really want to enjoy classic GTAs: find a PS2 and a copy of GTA Trilogy and enjoy the real masterpiece that R* created back in the good old days.

When you think of Rockstar Games, you think of quality content. When you think of GTA, you think of the best game ever made. It's a best-selling game that broke a lot of records and R* deserved it.... But that was almost 10 years ago. The mindset has changed a lot and the result can be seen today in GTA: The Trilogy: Definitive Edition. The goal of this remaster was to bring the classic titles to modern consoles and allow new players to enjoy the game as we did 20 years ago. But only in theory. What you get is actually not what you would expect from a GTA game, but the complete opposite. The graphics of the game seem new and beautiful for the first few minutes, but then you realize that the game hasn't been maintained at all. It's like "let's use Unreal because it has nice graphics, and just slap it on GTA III/VC/San Andreas" that's it. Sure, you can't just use a completely different engine, that requires some work.. Right? No, that's excatly how it looks like. All 3 games have the same bugs that you'd find in the original version of GTA. The remaster also introduced a lot of new bugs that just ruin the gameplay. The controls are really weird (especially in VC where it feels like you're playing the game on Stadia, Nvidia NOW, etc, but with a really bad internet connection). Some of the new textures are simply taken from GTA V, you can now see billboards with GTA: Online characters on them. A widescreen TV from the mid-2000s can now be found in GTA VC in Diaz mansion (the game is set in 1986).

And much more. That's just the tip of the iceberg, there's a lot more to tell, but I think most of it can easily be found on social media.

Would I recommend anyone to buy this game? No! If you really want to enjoy classic GTAs: find a PS2 and a copy of GTA Trilogy and enjoy the real masterpiece that R* created back in the good old days.

To me, the most special thing about RDR2 was that it shows us ecosystems that are changed or completely gone during the time when it was changing. RDR2 artfully tells us stories just by showing us the world that is at a turning point around us, and it goes beyond the buffalo being depleted by hunters, to landscapes that are being changed by dams redirecting bodies of water and logging. Noire was a very mature game with a deep story, brillant characters and a fantastic soundtrack. Yeah, the gameplay could have been better. The controls were not perfect. Invest your hard earned GTA dollars in the various businesses.

- Grind missions/heists/challenges until you get to $1m.
- Buy a cheap office and become a CEO.
- Grind CEO missions until you have a few hundred thousand dollars.
- Buy a warehouse
- Grind missions, but buy crates in between until warehouse is filled.
- sell all crates
- repeat until you get enough to either upgrade to a bigger warehouse or buy a clubhouse.
- grind club house missions until you get enough to by a weed/cocaine/forgery/meth business
- buy a weed business (less costly, fast earning, easy to fill)
- fill the weed business with supplies
- wait until the product is fully produced (in the meantime, grind crates and sell them)
- When product is full, sell all but beware of griefers.
- repeat the grinds, expand the business and multiply the funds until you're swimming in money.

Rockstar !!! Please don't forget about those who mostly play the OFFLINE story mode... After completing the story twice and having spent a total of ~200 hours exploring LS and doing side missions, there's not much left to do. I'm not so much interested in GTA Online (sorry lol) but here's what I'd like to see in the future updates for the offline mode to keep the experience fresh: 

- Car insurance for the offline mode. It's just pointless to purchase expansive vehicles only to lose or destroy them within minutes, and playing GTA "carefully" defeats the whole purpose, no? Please implement this ASAP, I'm sure I'm not the only person who wants it.

- No police cheat. Because sometimes it's just more fun to play without cops. Also a GTA Online lobby with no cops would be nice as well, but that's another story.

- Unlimited invincibility cheat. At present it's only 4 or 5 minutes of "God Mode", I don't even remember because I don't use it that much - it's just not as fun when you have to punch the code in every few minutes to active a cheat, and sometimes it's fun to do cause mayhem without worrying about dying, right? The time limit is so unnecessary...Why? lol.

- Easier way to input cheat codes. Not that the "phone numbers" are difficult to memorize, but it's a hassle to input them every time... You have to pull out the phone and go through the whole sequence of buttons just to get to the point where you can actually type them in. One way to fix this would be to allow players to input cheat codes via an external keyboard connected to the system - since it already works for browsing the in-game internet.. Or at least let us save the codes in the phone book after using them once or something. That'd make things so much better.

- Ability to turn off the music score during missions without having to turn off all music (including the radio) completely.

Thanks.

I think the reason San Andreas has an introduction is to demonstrate how San Andreas really connects to GTA 3 and Vice City. Ken was Tommy’s best friend, and Salvatore was Claude’s secondary antagonist, and additionally, it explains the balance of power between the families after Sonny’s death. It was also made to describe certain events in the story and give a better insight of Ryder’s betrayal. San Andreas is a good bridge between the two other games, even if it’s characters don’t appear that often. Still though it adds insight to their character development, especially Catalina and Salvatore, and what happens between Tommy and Ken, as well as setting up the story of GTA Liberty City Stories with the Mafia wars and Salvatore’s rather fragile position. We all love it because at the time it was extraordinary and special, and it was at the top of the gaming industry. Our nostalgic memories makes us love the game as we only started playing it yesterday.

Max Payne 3 not only stands the test of time - it improves with age - I've just replayed through on PC at 4K 120hz AA x4 using an LG C2 42 inch, the game certainly agrees with modern tech. Whilst I remember, it's clear that Max 3 inspired John Wick & Co. Everything about the game is utterly magnificent. The soundtrack, sound design, ambient SFX, art, gun-play, story, direction, character arc, mechanics...it's a marvel of game-craft & story execution, and it is a better game than previous two, of which I also adore. It's rare a film or games story & action starts well and becomes superior the further towards the end you get, simple or not. Those who have already completed know what I mean. The fizz you feel from walking into a nightclub to an airport - unparalleled in any game (think more fizz than the John Wick night club scene)! The previous games were superb but they did not deliver the moments awe that MP3 stokes. 

The noir, the gun-foo, the score, the OST, the story, the gritty truck-stop toilet that is Max's misfortune is undeniably back to and beyond, peak form with several changes of appearance (not one), location, alcohol branding and facial hair.

Make no mistake, this isn't just a legendary Payne entry - like Aliens it's an iconic entry that can stand alone - an instant classic that undoubtedly inspired more than gaming.

After replaying it for the 6th time since 2012 (it's now August 2023) I remain entirely sold. I played the first two once all the way through through. The impact was memorable, even iconic but the novelty wasn't enough to inspire multiple playthroughs. 

I've a very powerful editing suit. I maxed (pun intended) every setting, including AA on my rig. Wow! Just WOW! Every time I play the game is a revelation. It is also a more complete game than the previous in every metric let alone the fact that it has multiplayer and challenges. 

I'm baffled by the lack of overall love from the community and why some feel it's not good due to a few aesthetic changes whilst ignoring the fact that RockStar dialled everything way, way beyond the initial game and it's sequel. And MP3's story is not as basic as some make out. It is by far the most complex, which is why many don't understand/appreciate the editing and art style. 

I love the noir New York City stage. It's legendary. That said, MP3 is as good, if not better than the rest, if you remove nostalgia, and factor in the woeful amount of improvements and overall execution.

Objectively MP3 is one of, if not the greatest action games - of all-time. Gawd, there's so much I could say. I'm absolutely jazzed. Totally pumped. I think I'll go replay it again!

When I played GTA V, I found myself laughing at the three main character's collective pain, it was like non-stop comic relief, satire, and irony with little hints of drama. However playing Max Payne 3, I actually felt his pain. Max Payne's life story felt very real and established, and it was not a laughing matter. He was the like the embodiment of what death leaves behind. Being locked in his internal monologue provided huge insight into how he viewed himself: Max's mind wants him to lay down and die, but his body and instincts will not let him; and that is a torturous reality of depression and dysthymia. I think alot of people, no matter their station in life, feel dragged and kicked around by things that have happened and just want to give up, but something inside us keeps us going despite everything we do to sabotage ourselves. Deep down he wants to move on and truly live, but he has lived a life full of tragedy and failure for so long, that nothing else makes sense to him.

A great game. It took a few things that I liked from the first two though. 

-Graphic Novels
Yeah it's still a cinematic game, but I much prefer the comic book approach to story telling than full fledged cutscenes. It's a franchise trademark.

-Cover System
I understand Rockstar tried modernizing the game while remaining faithful, but the cover system isn't really necessary. The AI on normal difficulty are very accurate and very deadly, so not being behind cover more than 60% of the time means you'll die. A lot. That's a big departure from the constant action in the first two, where taking cover consisted of completely hiding behind a wall.

-Bullet time
Still awesome, still a lot of fun, and useful. However, it needlessly stripped the extra cinematics from Max Payne 2 that made it awesome. Remember the reload animations? Yeah, there's no reason why it's gone. It only added to the badass feel of the game. Bullet time now also seems a lot more risky, considering how I could grow a grey beard in the time it takes for Max to get up from a shoot dodge.

-Health and Painkillers
The game does live up to the challenge of the first two games. However, your health diminishes very quickly, and painkillers are rare. This heavily reduces the amount of risky badass shootouts the first two had, since half the time you're instantly killed when you expose your pinky. That goes back to the cover system, you have to resort to hiding and waiting for enemies to show their faces. This game has quite a lot of frustrating deaths.

-Aiming
The aiming reticle isn't centered with the character anymore, and the auto view swapping after bullet time is very frustrating. I wish it were only mapped to the button so I don't constantly have to change it. 

-Controls
No custom controls? No classic controls? Really Rockstar? Ah well.

All those aside, I love the game. :D

Things GTA 4 did well:
-Comedy (humurous characters and cutscenes)
-Character (story/background/personality)
-Friends (Actually cared about going out for drinks or bowling etc...)
-Mood (Darken mood for a dark character and a deep story)
-Choices (Choices that impacted the main story i.e.-Executions)
-Random Events (Finding people from Niko's past)
-Random Events (Findng new people of Liberty City)
-Random Events (Finding the people you left alive in the choices)
-Immersion (I actually felt immersed in the city. I would often just sit in the couch watching TV)
-The Stand up Comedy show (Split sides) It was awesome!!!
-Story (A great story with different outcomes, different plots, twists, and overall great writting)
-Dating (It was fun to pick a girlfriend from the websites and go on dates)
-Emails (The emails Niko received AND sent were awesome and meaningful AND you could see him writing it them)
-Cyber Cafes (It was cool to actually have to go to an internet cafe to check the email AND visit that girl that worked there :)
-Meaningful dates (Going out with girls OR friends was always awesome and had interesting conversation topics)
-Meaningful dates (The people were different and so it was always interesting to hear from them and their stories)
-Cool places (Going out the bro's or with the GF was always awesome, there were always cool places to visit like:
- Restaurants (Characters would comment on if they liked the place or not)
- Bowling (Bowling was a fun minigame especially to share with the company)
- Pool (Pool is another great minigame to play with the bros)
- Comedy show & Cabaret club (these were AMAZING to go to and see a show!!! Funny & interesting)
-----------

There are many things that GTA 4 did very well, these things I pointed above are NOWHERE TO BE SEEN in GTA 5 which is a shame. Obviously GTA 5 has "friends" and "comedy" but not like GTA 4 did.
Even though GTA 5 is a great game and much more fun to play (open world etc) it will never have the impact (emotional, immersive, etc) that GTA 4 has.
For instance... I could give a fuck about Michael, Trevor or Franklin... And much less of Lamar... Ron... Wade... etc. 
However I LOVED Niko bellic, Patrick McReary, Little Jacob, Dwayne, Kate, Gerry, Derrick, Roman, Brucie, Michelle, etc.etc.etc.. So much that I actually SHITTED myself when I saw Packie was in GTA 5.
I respect and love GTA 5, including all the work that was put into making it be a masterpiece BUT I get a little mad and annoyed at why Rockstar didn't grab those good things in GTA 4 and brough them to GTA 5...
This makes GTA 5 a great journey with awesome missions and great fun to be had but not much else... 
In a few years I will still remember the story and characters AND feeling of when I played GTA 4 but as for GTA 5 I will probably only remember the protagonists and not much else.
